title: The fate of $s_{\pm}$ superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$
abstract: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an $s_\pm$ superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like $d$-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full $SU(2)$ particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual $U(1)$ treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of $s_\pm$ symmetry in favor of $d$-wave pairing.
summary: This theoretical work investigates the superconducting pairing symmetry in bilayer nickelates using a sophisticated mean-field fractionalization approach on the $t$-$J$ model. By rigorously enforcing the local no-double-occupancy constraint via $	ext{SU}(2)$ symmetry, the authors demonstrate that the resulting physics favors $d$-wave pairing over the $s_{\pm}$ state. This highlights the critical role of local constraints in determining high-temperature superconductivity mechanisms.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the role of interlayer coupling in dictating the superconducting pairing symmetry ($s_{\pm}$ vs. $d$-wave) in the bilayer nickelate $	ext{La}_3	ext{Ni}_2	ext{O}_7$.
main_result: The authors show that by incorporating a full $	ext{SU}(2)$ symmetry treatment that enforces the local no-double-occupancy constraint, the resulting Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the $s_{\pm}$ symmetry in favor of $d$-wave pairing.
method: The study employs a mean-field fractionalization treatment applied to a simplified bilayer $t$-$J$ model, which captures the full $	ext{SU}(2)$ symmetry.
model_or_system: The physical system is the bilayer nickelate $	ext{La}_3	ext{Ni}_2	ext{O}_7$, modeled using a projected bilayer $t$-$J$ Hamiltonian. The analysis focuses on how local constraints, absent in simpler $	ext{U}(1)$ treatments, affect the pairing state.
key_observables: Pairing symmetry ($s_{\pm}$ vs. $d$-wave), superconducting gap structure, and the effect of the Coulomb pseudopotential.
important_parameters: Interlayer coupling, hopping terms ($t$), and superexchange couplings ($J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a mean-field approximation on a simplified bilayer $t$-$J$ model, focusing on the effect of the local no-double-occupancy constraint.
figures_summary: Figures compare $d$-wave and $s_{\pm}$-wave pairing orders and illustrate the competition between pairing channels under different coupling regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops a mean-field fractionalization scheme capturing $	ext{SU}(2)$ symmetry, derives a new Coulomb pseudopotential constraint, and then applies this to the bilayer $t$-$J$ model to predict the favored pairing symmetry.
why_interesting: The explicit inclusion of local constraints via $	ext{SU}(2)$ symmetry provides a rigorous theoretical tool to analyze pairing competition in strongly correlated systems, which is relevant for understanding exotic pairing mechanisms beyond standard BCS theory.
